name: @kolu/acp-harness
//exports: ONE door, and it is one on purpose: a second subpath would be a second way to reach a subprocess, and there is exactly one subprocess. What the door now hands out beside `startHarness` is the conversation layer itself — `Transcript`, `Turns`, the held list, and the `says`/`plus` rules over a change — because two products run one conversation each and both must be served by the same classes rather than by a copy in each.
//scripts: `test:daemon`, not `test:unit`: every test here but one spawns a real ACP agent as a detached process group (the fixture agents `@kolu/acp-client/testlib` hands out), which is the lane `just test-daemon` runs serially and `just test-unit` skips — the same reason `kolu-omp` declares it. A package declares ONE lane, so the pure `src/kolu.test.ts` rides along in it.
//dependencies: THE ONE PACKAGE IN THIS TREE THAT RUNS THE PROTOCOL, so the SDK is a RUNTIME dependency here and a type-only one in `@kolu/acp` (`packages/acp/src/manifest.test.ts` holds both halves). `kolu-common` is imported for the row and state TYPES alone — the harness writes that contract and never reaches for a daemon itself. `kolu-mcp` is reached ONLY at its `/fleetRef` leaf, which is the one definition of the `host/id` grammar a kolu call's args are written in; that subpath deliberately carries no MCP SDK and no padi-client, so the manifest above stays true. `@kolu/terminal-vocab` is reached ONLY at its `/terminalId` leaf, for `isTerminalId`: a string the agent wrote becomes a card's terminal only if it passes the same check the wire's row schema applies, so the reading and the encoder cannot disagree. That leaf's one import is effect — the only piece of effect this package's runtime carries. `@kolu/child` is a LEAF beside `@kolu/log`: the subprocess socket, with no dependency of its own, so the adapter and the sign-in command are started by one definition rather than a second copy here.
//devDependencies: `effect` for `src/kolu.test.ts` alone, which encodes readings under the contract's row schema — the check production leaves to the host that publishes the rows. `@kolu/acp-client` for its `./testlib` alone: every fixture agent lives there, beside the client whose protocol they speak.
